section.sectionSummaryBrief: The discourse questions why joy and gladness precede mention of groom and bride in the blessing, and why the term "created" is used for supernal groom and bride.
section.t: precisely asks: why does it preface joy and gladness before groom and bride,
is that which makes the groom and bride rejoice, as per the statement39
"How does one dance before the bride?"
regarding what is said: "which He created... groom and bride,"
for since the beginning of the concept of groom and bride is the supernal groom and bride,
how can one say about this "which He created,"
is included among the Sefiros of Atzilus
"the peace of the faithful of Israel"43],
and certainly regarding the supernal groom, who is Zeir Anpin,
how can the term "creation" be said of him?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: It explains the difficulty with the verse "Before Me no god was formed," questioning how the term "formation" applies to the name Kel.
section.t: And it explains44 by prefacing what is said45
how the term "formation" can apply to the name Kel, which is one of the names of the Holy One, blessed be He,
from the seven names that are not erased47.
And the precision in this verse is even greater than the precision in the blessing "which He created,"

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation is that the name Kel relates to worlds, as it is associated with Chesed, the foundation of world-building, and similarly the term "creation" applies to the groom because "groom" implies descent.
section.t: that the name Kel pertains to the worlds.
For the name Kel is in Chesed48,
and regarding the matter of Chesed it is written49
"For I said, 'The world is built with kindness,'"
the intent being that the building of the world is through the Sefirah of Chesed, and that the building of the Sefirah of Chesed is for the sake of the coming-into-being of the worlds50.
Therefore, the term "formation" applies to the name Kel, as it is the source for the worlds.
it is also regarding the aspect of the groom
for "groom" is from the term "Chot Darga"52
[for although the distinction between Zeir Anpin
is that Malchus, even as it is in Atzilus, is the root and source of Biyah, unlike Zeir Anpin which is the end of the worlds of the Ein Sof
nevertheless, "groom" is from the term "Chot Darga"],
and therefore the term "creation" applies to him.
